title: Patient Payment Plan Grace Days, Default Point and Assistance Pause Days by Tier
content:
These figures govern missed installments on the **Patient Payment Plan**. Grace days are the calendar days after an installment due date before the installment counts as missed. The default point is the number of consecutive missed installments at which a past-due plan defaults. The default notice period is the calendar days between the default notice and the earliest collection action on the plan's encounters. The assistance pause days are the calendar days installments may be paused while a financial assistance application is pending.

| Tier | Grace days | Consecutive missed installments at default | Default notice period (calendar days) | Assistance pause days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Riverbend Short-Term Payment Plan | 10 | 2 | 30 | 60 |
| Riverbend Standard Payment Plan | 10 | 2 | 30 | 60 |
| Riverbend Extended Payment Plan | 15 | 2 | 30 | 60 |
| Riverbend Long-Term Payment Plan | 15 | 3 | 30 | 60 |
| Riverbend Assistance-Linked Payment Plan | 20 | 3 | 30 | 90 |
| Riverbend Hardship Payment Plan | 30 | 3 | 30 | 90 |

## Points of comparison

- A plan on the Extended tier that has missed 2 consecutive installments has reached its default point; a plan on the Long-Term tier with the same 2 missed installments has not, because its default point is 3.
- Grace runs 10 calendar days on the Short-Term and Standard tiers and 30 on the Hardship tier.
